items.title: 5.2.1 Transform the General Linear Equation to Standard Forms (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 143-145: 5.2.1 Theorem 2, (i)-(vi) six standard forms with normal-form proof; Example 6; Challenge! box

blocks.text: Pichhle safhe par humne saabit kiya ke \(ax + by + c = 0\) hamesha seedhi line hai. Ab is line ko hum Section 5.1 wali tamaam standard forms mein badalna seekhenge. Yeh bilkul aisa hai jaise ek hi raqam ko rupay, paison ya dollar mein likhna: raqam wohi, sirf likhne ka andaz alag.
Theorem 2: Equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) ko standard forms mein badalna.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Badalne ki zaroorat kyun? Har standard form line ki koi ek khasiyat foran dikha deti hai: slope-intercept form slope aur y-intercept dikhati hai; intercept form batati hai ke line axes ko kahan kaat-ti hai; normal form origin se faasla batati hai. Har hisse mein tareeqa ek hi hai: \(ax + by + c = 0\) ko itna rearrange (tarteeb badalna) karo ke woh bilkul matloob form jaisi lagne lage, phir constants parh lo.
(i) Slope-Intercept Form

Hamare paas hai
\[ax + by + c = 0\]
ya
\[by = -ax - c\]
ya
\[y = -\dfrac{a}{b}x - \dfrac{c}{b} = mx + k\]
(jahan \(b \neq 0\)), aur
\[m = -\dfrac{a}{b}, \quad k = -\dfrac{c}{b}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan \(b\) se taqseem kiya hai, is liye \(b \neq 0\) ki shart lagayi. Agar \(b = 0\) ho to line vertical hai aur us ki slope-intercept form banti hi nahi.

Ab doosri form. Point-slope form ko do cheezein chahiye: ek point aur slope. Slope hum (i) mein nikal chuke hain; ab sirf ek point chahiye. Line ka sab se aasaan point dhoondne ka tareeqa hai ek coordinate ko zero rakh dena.
(ii) Point-Slope Form

Upar se humein pata hai ke line \(ax + by + c = 0\) ka slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) aur y-intercept \(-\frac{c}{b}\) hai. Point \((-\frac{c}{a}, 0)\) line par hai.
Point-slope form mein line ki equation:
\[y - 0 = -\dfrac{a}{b}\left(x + \dfrac{c}{a}\right)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Point \((-\frac{c}{a}, 0)\) kahan se aaya? \(ax + by + c = 0\) mein \(y = 0\) rakhiye: \(ax + c = 0\), yani \(x = -\frac{c}{a}\) (is ke liye \(a \neq 0\) chahiye). Yeh x-intercept wala point hai. Line ka koi bhi point chalega; misaal ke taur par \((0, -\frac{c}{b})\) lein to \(y + \frac{c}{b} = -\frac{a}{b}x\) milta hai, jo wohi line hai.

Ab teesri form, symmetric form. Yeh shayad aap ke liye nayi ho, is liye dhyan se suniye. Is form mein line ko ek point aur ek direction (simt) se likha jata hai, jaise kisi ko rasta samjhate hue kehte hain: is chowk se shuru karo aur seedha shimal-mashriq ki taraf chalte jao. Chowk point hai, simt direction hai, aur kitna chale, woh r hai.
(iii) Symmetric Form

\[\dfrac{x - x_{1}}{\cos\theta} = \dfrac{y - y_{1}}{\sin\theta}\]
\[= r \text{ (say)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Symmetric form ka matlab samajhiye: \(\theta\) line ka inclination hai aur \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) line ka ek point. Is point se line ke saath saath \(r\) faasla chalein to hum is point par pohanchte hain:
\[x = x_{1} + r\cos\theta, \quad y = y_{1} + r\sin\theta\]
Dono ko \(r\) ke liye hal karein to do barabar fractions milte hain. Yani \(r\) point \((x, y)\) ka \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) se faasla hai (sign ke saath), aur \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) line ki direction hai. Is liye zaroori hai ke \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = m\) ho. Jaise sarak par chalne wale ko pata ho ke kis simt (direction) mein kitna chalna hai.

Slope \(m = \tan\theta = -\frac{a}{b}\) hai, is liye (radical ka ek hi sign dono jagah)
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{-a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
\(ax + by + c = 0\) par ek point \((-\frac{c}{a}, 0)\) hai.
Lihaza symmetric form mein line ki equation:
\[\dfrac{x - \left(-\frac{c}{a}\right)}{\frac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}} = r\]
\[\dfrac{y - 0}{\frac{-a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}} = r\]
Radical ka sign theek tarah chuna jaye (dono jagah ek hi).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab \(\sin\theta = \frac{a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\), \(\cos\theta = \frac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\) chhapti hai, aur phir symmetric form mein \(y - 0\) ke neeche \(a\) likhti hai. In values se \(\tan\theta = \frac{a}{b}\) banta hai, jabke slope \(m = \tan\theta = -\frac{a}{b}\) hai. Yani \(\sin\theta\) ka sign ghalat hai. Sahi values (dono mein radical ka ek hi sign):
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{-a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
aur symmetric form mein \(y - 0\) ke neeche \(\frac{-a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\) aata hai. Test: \(x - y = 0\) (\(a = 1\), \(b = -1\), slope 1). Sahi formula direction \((\mp\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \mp\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})\) deta hai, slope 1; kitab wala \((\mp\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})\), slope \(-1\), yani bilkul doosri line. Neeche Example 6 (vi) mein kitab ne khud sahi signs istemal kiye hain.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Line \(y = x\) ki symmetric form kya hogi agar point \((0, 0)\) lein? Slope 1 hai, yani \(\theta = 45^\circ\), \(\cos\theta = \sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Form: \(\frac{x - 0}{1/\sqrt{2}} = \frac{y - 0}{1/\sqrt{2}} = r\). Point \((1, 1)\) ke liye \(r = \sqrt{2}\), jo bilkul origin se \((1, 1)\) ka faasla hai. Dekha, \(r\) sach mein faasla hai!
(iv) Two-Point Form

\(ax + by + c = 0\) par koi do points chunte hain. Do aise points \((-\frac{c}{a}, 0)\) aur \((0, -\frac{c}{b})\) hain. In points se guzarne wali line ki equation:
\[\dfrac{y - 0}{0 + \frac{c}{b}} = \dfrac{x + \frac{c}{a}}{-\frac{c}{a} - 0}\]
ya
\[y - 0 = \dfrac{\frac{c}{b}}{-\frac{c}{a}}\left(x + \dfrac{c}{a}\right)\]
ya
\[y = -\dfrac{a}{b}\left(x + \dfrac{c}{a}\right)\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan two-point form \(\frac{y - y_{1}}{y_{1} - y_{2}} = \frac{x - x_{1}}{x_{1} - x_{2}}\) istemal hui hai, jahan \((x_{1}, y_{1}) = (-\frac{c}{a}, 0)\) aur \((x_{2}, y_{2}) = (0, -\frac{c}{b})\). Beech wale qadam mein \(\frac{c/b}{-c/a} = \frac{c}{b} \times \frac{a}{-c} = -\frac{a}{b}\), yani wohi slope. Shart: \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) teeno non-zero hon. Agar \(c = 0\) ho to dono points origin ban jate hain, aur ek point se line fix nahi hoti. Tab koi aur point lijiye, jaise \(x = 1\), \(y = -\frac{a}{b}\).

Ab intercept form. Yahan sawal yeh hai ke line x-axis aur y-axis ko kahan kaat-ti hai. Socho ek seedhi sarak do baraabar wali galiyon (axes) ko kaat rahi hai; intercept form seedha bata deti hai ke kis kis jagah se guzarti hai.
(v) Two-Intercept Form

\[ax + by = -c\]
ya
\[\dfrac{ax}{-c} + \dfrac{by}{-c} = 1\]
ya
\[\dfrac{x}{\left(-\frac{c}{a}\right)} + \dfrac{y}{\left(-\frac{c}{b}\right)} = 1\]
jahan x-intercept \(= -\frac{c}{a}\), y-intercept \(= -\frac{c}{b}\). Yahi two-intercept form mein line ki equation hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Do chhote qadam: pehle \(-c\) se taqseem kiya taake right side 1 ban jaye (is ke liye \(c \neq 0\)); phir \(\frac{ax}{-c}\) ko \(\frac{x}{-c/a}\) likha, kyunke \(\frac{-c}{a}\) se taqseem karna aur \(\frac{a}{-c}\) se multiply karna ek hi baat hai.

Aakhri aur sab se ahem form: normal form. Is ka faida yeh hai ke is se foran pata chal jata hai ke line origin se kitni door hai. Aage distance ke sawalon mein yahi kaam aayegi. Yahan sab se ahem cheez radical ka sign chunna hai, is liye har qadam ghor se dekhiye.
(vi) Normal Form

Equation
\[ax + by + c = 0 \quad \ldots(i)\]
ko normal form mein yun likha ja sakta hai:
\[\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} \quad \ldots(ii)\]
Radical ka sign aisa chuna jaye ke (ii) ki right hand side positive ho.

Proof: Hum jaante hain ke normal form mein line ki equation hai:
\[x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p \quad \ldots(iii)\]
Agar (i) aur (iii) ek hi line hain, to zaroori hai ke
\[\dfrac{a}{\cos\theta} = \dfrac{b}{\sin\theta} = -\dfrac{c}{p}\]
yani
\[\dfrac{p}{-c} = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{a} = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{b}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta}}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{1}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
Lihaza
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}, \quad \sin\theta = \dfrac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
aur
\[p = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
\(\cos\theta\), \(\sin\theta\) aur \(p\) ki values (iii) mein rakhne se:
\[\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\]
Yani (i) ko \(\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) se taqseem kar ke form (ii) mil jati hai. Radical ka sign aisa chunein ke (ii) ki right hand side positive ho.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
'Ek hi line' ka matlab yeh kyun ke coefficients proportional hon? Ek line ki do equations mein sirf ek constant factor ka farq ho sakta hai (jaise \(x + y = 2\) aur \(3x + 3y = 6\)). Is liye corresponding coefficients ki ratios barabar hoti hain. (i) ko \(ax + by = -c\) likh kar \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\) se milaiye.
\(\sqrt{\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta}\) wala qadam is usool par hai: agar \(\frac{u}{a} = \frac{v}{b} = k\) ho to \(u = ka\), \(v = kb\), is liye \(\sqrt{u^{2} + v^{2}} = |k|\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\). Aur \(\cos^{2}\theta + \sin^{2}\theta = 1\) hamesha.
Sign ka aasaan usool: agar \(c < 0\) ho to \(+\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) se taqseem karein; agar \(c > 0\) ho to \(-\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) se. Phir \(p = \frac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\), jo origin se line ka faasla hai. Yeh formula aage bohat kaam aayega.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Normal form ki ek aur misaal, jahan \(c\) positive hai: \(3x + 4y + 10 = 0\).
Pehle constant ko right side bhejiye: \(3x + 4y = -10\). Right side negative hai, is liye radical ka negative sign lena hoga: \(-\sqrt{9 + 16} = -5\) se taqseem.
\[-\dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{4}{5}y = 2\]
Yahan \(p = 2\), \(\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}\), \(\sin\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\). Dono negative hain, is liye perpendicular third quadrant mein hai (\(\theta \approx 233.1^\circ\)). Tasdeeq: origin se faasla \(\frac{|10|}{5} = 2\). Bilkul wohi.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Paper mein jab 'transform into all forms' aaye, to sab se pehle ek kachi line mein yeh teen cheezein likh lijiye: slope \(m = -\frac{a}{b}\), x-intercept \(-\frac{c}{a}\), y-intercept \(-\frac{c}{b}\), aur \(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\). Phir har form sirf in ko jagah par rakhne ka kaam reh jati hai. Is se waqt bhi bachta hai aur har form mein ek hi numbers aate hain, to ghalti ka imkaan kam ho jata hai. Har form ke neeche us ka naam saaf likhiye, kyunke examiner part-wise marks deta hai.

Ab Example 6 dekhte hain. Is mein ek hi line ko chhe forms mein badalna hai. Ghabraiye nahi; har form ke liye wohi teen cheezein chahiye: slope, ek ya do points, aur thori si algebra. Pehle slope aur intercepts nikal lijiye, baqi kaam khud aasaan ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem:
Transform the equation \(3x - 10y + 13 = 0\) into
(i) Slope-intercept form (ii) Two-intercept form (iii) Normal form (iv) Point-slope form (v) Two-point form (vi) Symmetric form
steps:
Diya gaya: \(3x - 10y + 13 = 0\), yani \(a = 3\), \(b = -10\), \(c = 13\).
Maloom karna: isi line ko chhe (6) standard forms mein likhna.
Tareeqa: Theorem 2 ko hissa ba hissa follow karna hai. Zyada tar forms ko slope \(m = -\frac{a}{b} = -\frac{3}{-10} = \frac{3}{10}\) aur line par ek ya do points chahiye. Yeh cheezein hum saath saath nikalte jayenge.

(i) Slope-intercept form
\[3x - 10y + 13 = 0\]
\[10y = 3x + 13\]
\[y = \dfrac{3}{10}x + \dfrac{13}{10}\]
jahan \(m = \frac{3}{10}\), \(c = \frac{13}{10}\).
Kyun: \(y\) wale term ko ek taraf akela chhora (baqi sab doosri taraf bheja, jahan sign badal gaya), phir us ke coefficient 10 se taqseem kiya. Ab \(x\) ke saath wala number slope hai aur akela number y-intercept.

(ii) Two-intercept form
\[3x - 10y = -13\]
\[\dfrac{3x}{-13} + \dfrac{10}{13}y = 1\]
\[\dfrac{x}{-\frac{13}{3}} + \dfrac{y}{\frac{13}{10}} = 1\]
Kyun: is form mein right side 1 honi chahiye, is liye poori equation ko \(-13\) se taqseem kiya. Phir har coefficient ko 'neeche ke neeche' bhej diya: \(\frac{3x}{-13} = \frac{x}{-13/3}\). Intercepts \(-\frac{13}{3}\) aur \(\frac{13}{10}\) hain.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{-10y}{-13} = +\frac{10y}{13}\); minus taqseem minus plus hota hai.

(iii) Normal form: radical se taqseem
\[3x - 10y = -13\]
Dono taraf ko is se taqseem karte hain:
\[\pm\sqrt{(3)^{2} + (-10)^{2}} = \pm\sqrt{109}\]
Kyunke R.H.S. positive hona chahiye, is liye negative sign lena hoga.
Kyun: normal form mein right side \(p\) hai, jo ek faasla hai, aur faasla kabhi negative nahi hota. R.H.S. \(-13\) hai; \(-\sqrt{109}\) se taqseem karne par yeh \(+\frac{13}{\sqrt{109}}\) ban jata hai.

(iii) Normal form: natija
\[-\dfrac{3x}{\sqrt{109}} + \dfrac{10y}{\sqrt{109}} = \dfrac{13}{\sqrt{109}}\]
Yahi di gayi equation ki normal form hai.
Kyun: ab \(\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{\sqrt{109}}\), \(\sin\theta = \frac{10}{\sqrt{109}}\) (in ke squares ka jor \(\frac{9 + 100}{109} = 1\)), aur \(p = \frac{13}{\sqrt{109}} \approx 1.245\). \(\cos\theta\) negative aur \(\sin\theta\) positive hai, is liye \(\theta\) second quadrant mein hai: \(\theta \approx 106.7^\circ\).

(iv) Point-slope form
Line par ek point \((-\frac{13}{3}, 0)\) hai aur slope \(\frac{3}{10}\) hai.
\[y - 0 = \dfrac{3}{10}\left(x + \dfrac{13}{3}\right)\]
Kyun: equation mein \(y = 0\) rakhne se \(3x + 13 = 0\), yani \(x = -\frac{13}{3}\); slope part (i) se mil chuka hai. Point-slope form ko bas yahi do cheezein chahiye.

(v) Two-point form
Line par koi do points lete hain: \((-\frac{13}{3}, 0)\) aur \((0, \frac{13}{10})\).
\[\dfrac{y - 0}{\frac{13}{10} - 0} = \dfrac{x + \frac{13}{3}}{0 + \frac{13}{3}}\]
Kyun: sab se aasaan points intercepts wale hote hain: pehle \(y = 0\) rakho, phir \(x = 0\). \(x = 0\) par \(-10y + 13 = 0\), yani \(y = \frac{13}{10}\).

(vi) Symmetric form: direction nikaliye
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{10} = m\]
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{109}}, \quad \cos\theta = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{109}}\]
aur line par ek point \((-\frac{13}{3}, 0)\) hai.
Kyun: yahan \(\theta\) line ka inclination (jhukao) hai. Aisa right triangle sochiye jis ki base 10 aur perpendicular 3 ho; hypotenuse \(\sqrt{100 + 9} = \sqrt{109}\). Slope positive hai, is liye \(\theta\) acute (90 se chhota) lete hain aur sin, cos dono positive.

(vi) Symmetric form: natija
\[\dfrac{x + \frac{13}{3}}{\frac{10}{\sqrt{109}}} = \dfrac{y - 0}{\frac{3}{\sqrt{109}}}\]
\[= r \text{ (say)}\]
Kyun: form \(\frac{x - x_{1}}{\cos\theta} = \frac{y - y_{1}}{\sin\theta} = r\) hai, jahan \((x_{1}, y_{1}) = (-\frac{13}{3}, 0)\). Ghor kijiye ke yahan neeche \(y\) wali taraf 3 hai, jo \(-a\) wale sahi formula se milta hai (radical ka negative sign le kar).

Tasdeeq:
(ii) ko \(-\frac{3x}{13} + \frac{10y}{13} = 1\) likh kar 13 se multiply karein: \(-3x + 10y = 13\), wohi line.
(vi) ko cross-multiply karein: \(3(x + \frac{13}{3}) = 10y\), yani \(3x - 10y + 13 = 0\). Har form wapas di gayi equation ban jati hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Part (iii) mein agar hum galti se \(+\sqrt{109}\) se taqseem kar dete to kya hota? Right side \(-\frac{13}{\sqrt{109}}\) aata, yani \(p\) negative, jo faasla nahi ho sakta. Is liye sign ka faisla hamesha right side dekh kar kijiye.

blocks.title: Challenge!
blocks.text: Equation \(2x + 5y - 10 = 0\) ko slope-intercept form, two-intercept form, normal form, point-slope form, two-point form aur symmetric form mein badaliye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir hamare jawabon se milaiye:
Slope-intercept: \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 2\).
Two-intercept: \(\frac{x}{5} + \frac{y}{2} = 1\).
Normal (yahan \(c = -10 < 0\), is liye \(+\sqrt{29}\) se taqseem): \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}}x + \frac{5}{\sqrt{29}}y = \frac{10}{\sqrt{29}}\).
Point-slope (point \((5, 0)\)): \(y - 0 = -\frac{2}{5}(x - 5)\).
Two-point (points \((5, 0)\), \((0, 2)\)): \(\frac{y - 0}{2 - 0} = \frac{x - 5}{0 - 5}\).
Symmetric (\(\cos\theta = \frac{5}{\sqrt{29}}\), \(\sin\theta = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{29}}\), kyunke slope negative hai): \(\frac{x - 5}{5/\sqrt{29}} = \frac{y - 0}{-2/\sqrt{29}} = r\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Slope \(m = -\frac{a}{b}\); x-intercept \(-\frac{c}{a}\); y-intercept \(-\frac{c}{b}\). Taqreeban har form inhi teen numbers se banti hai.
2. Intercept form: \(-c\) se taqseem kar ke right side 1 banaiye.
3. Normal form: \(\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) se taqseem; sign aisa ke right side positive ho.
4. Symmetric form: \(\cos\theta\), \(\sin\theta\) se \(\tan\theta = m\) aana chahiye; \(\cos\theta = \frac{b}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\), \(\sin\theta = \frac{-a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\).
5. Har form ko simplify kar ke wapas \(ax + by + c = 0\) bana kar check kijiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Normal form mein radical ka sign left side dekh kar chunna; usool sirf ek hai: right side positive.
2. Intercept ka minus bhool jana: \(3x - 10y + 13 = 0\) ka x-intercept \(-\frac{13}{3}\) hai.
3. Kitab wala \(\sin\theta = \frac{a}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\) symmetric form mein laga dena: is se direction ka slope \(\frac{a}{b}\) aata hai, ulta sign.
4. \(c = 0\) hone par bhi intercept wale points se two-point form banana (dono origin hain).
